_metadata.purpose: Illustrative walkthrough: how the same Python file is processed by (1) Pretrained models under C0-C4, and (2) the GNN — whose input is invariant. Based on actual pipeline code in src/data/obfuscation.py and src/data/subtree_extractor.py.
_metadata.note: This is a hand-constructed example that faithfully follows the real pipeline. The domain sample files (domain_*.json, appendix_E*.json) show the actual GNN input format.

step1_uast_parsing.description: Step 1: Python source → UAST JSON (via tree-sitter). The UAST stores structural nodes — the 'code_snippet' field records what construct was parsed.
step1_uast_parsing.example_python_source:
# A scientific computing file (synthetic illustration)
import numpy as np
from scipy import signal

def process_signal(data, window_size):
    filtered = signal.savgol_filter(data, window_size, 3)
    result = np.fft.fft(filtered)
    return result

def compute_spectrum(samples, rate):
    freqs = np.fft.fftfreq(len(samples), 1.0 / rate)
    power = np.abs(samples) ** 2
    return freqs, power

step2_pretrained_model_path.description: Step 2a (Pretrained model path): obfuscation.py reconstruct_code_text() extracts import lines and function names from the UAST as a code-like text string. This string is what CodeBERT / GraphCodeBERT / TF-IDF tokenize. C1-C4 apply progressive token replacement to this string only.
step2_pretrained_model_path.reconstructed_text_C0:
import numpy
import scipy.signal
def process_signal(): pass
def compute_spectrum(): pass

C0.label: Clean (0% obfuscation)
C0.text_input_to_pretrained_model:
import numpy
import scipy.signal
def process_signal(): pass
def compute_spectrum(): pass
C0.domain_signal_strength: Strong — library names (numpy, scipy) are highly discriminative

C1.label: Import masking only — library names replaced
C1.text_input_to_pretrained_model:
import LIB_a3f2b1
import LIB_c8d4e9
def process_signal(): pass
def compute_spectrum(): pass
C1.domain_signal_strength: Weak — libraries gone; function names still carry some signal

C2.label: Identifier stripping only — non-library names replaced
C2.text_input_to_pretrained_model:
import numpy
import scipy.signal
def ID_m3n4o5(): pass
def ID_v2w3x4(): pass
C2.domain_signal_strength: Moderate — libraries still visible; function semantics lost

C3.label: Partial obfuscation — 50% of unique tokens replaced
C3.text_input_to_pretrained_model:
import numpy
import OBF_h4i5j6
def OBF_k7l8m9(): pass
def compute_spectrum(): pass
C3.domain_signal_strength: Partial — degraded but residual signal present

C4.label: Full obfuscation — 100% of unique tokens replaced
C4.text_input_to_pretrained_model:
import OBF_a1b2c3
import OBF_d4e5f6
def OBF_g7h8i9(): pass
def OBF_j0k1l2(): pass
C4.domain_signal_strength: None — all surface-form signal is destroyed

step2_gnn_path.description: Step 2b (GNN path): subtree_extractor.py encode_node_features() converts each node to a one-hot vector over 6 node types. The identifier in code_snippet is NOT used — only the node_type prefix is encoded. This representation is therefore IDENTICAL across C0-C4.

gnn_input.description: What the GNN actually receives — identical for C0, C1, C2, C3, C4. The actual domain sample files (domain_*.json, appendix_E*.json in this directory) show real examples of this format.
gnn_input.invariance_note: The one-hot features and edge_index above are IDENTICAL whether the input was the C0 Python source or C4 fully-obfuscated source — because identifiers are never part of the feature encoding. This is why GNN Retention = C4_acc / C0_acc = 1.000 (Table 1, §3.2).
